extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, startups, and individual bloggers/journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and resources for newsrooms, startups, and individual journalists to create a bespoke ethics code that reflects their values and operational needs for online journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should have ownership and flexibility in creating an ethics code that meets their needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'This project aims to provide journalists and news organizations with the ownership and flexibility in creating an ethics code that meets their needs in our widely varied profession.' Emphasizes that codes should be created/adopted by the organization and be adaptable to its circumstances rather than one-size-fits-all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflects organization’s journalistic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: An ethics code should reflect the newsroom's own journalistic principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: 'designed to help news organizations, startups and individual bloggers and journalists create codes that reflect their own journalistic principles.' Implies criteria: alignment with declared values, mission, and practices of the organization or individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical comprehensiveness (coverage of relevant online issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics codes should address a range of topics relevant to online journalism, such as clickbait, metrics, data journalism, online commenting, archive removal, and social networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed on the page under 'Topics Covered in the Project': 'Clickbait and metrics; Data journalism; Online commenting; Removing material from your archives; Social networks; And dozens more.' Implies guidance to cover current online-specific ethical issues and other topics relevant to the organization's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptable for different scales and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and resulting codes should be usable by a variety of actors, from large news organizations to startups and individual bloggers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project is described as supporting 'news organizations, startups and individual bloggers and journalists,' indicating that the code templates/guidance should be scalable and adaptable to different sizes, resources, and publication formats.
